questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of the complex ion [Pt(NH₃)BrCl(NO₂)]⁻, in which the nitrite ligand is bonded through nitrogen, is:

solution.explanation: The ligands are named in alphabetical order: ammine, bromido, chlorido, nitrito-N. The oxidation state of platinum is x + 0 − 1 − 1 − 1 = −1, so x = +2. Because the entity is an anion, the metal name takes the ending -ate: platinate(II).
steps: Ligands alphabetically: ammine (a), bromido (b), chlorido (c), nitrito-N (n)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Platinum(II)' is used only when the entity is a cation or neutral; chlorido before bromido breaks the alphabetical order; (IV) ignores the three anionic ligands in the charge balance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', naming of mononuclear coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The formula of dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate is:

solution.concept: Writing the formula from the name
solution.explanation: The coordination entity contains two chloride ions and two neutral en ligands around Pt⁴⁺, so its charge is +4 − 2 = +2. Two nitrate ions balance this charge.
solution.why_others_wrong: One or four nitrate ions do not balance a +2 entity; writing the chlorides outside the square brackets contradicts the name, which lists them as ligands (dichlorido).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', formulas of mononuclear coordination entities

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following coordination entities are heteroleptic?
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺, [Ni(CO)₄], [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺, [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], [Cr(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻, [Co(NH₃)₅(H₂O)]³⁺

solution.explanation: A complex in which the metal is bound to only one kind of donor group is homoleptic; one bound to more than one kind of donor group is heteroleptic.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 usually misses [Co(NH₃)₅(H₂O)]³⁺, where one water molecule makes the complex heteroleptic; 5 or 6 counts charged or chelate complexes such as [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ or [Cr(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻, which have only one kind of ligand.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', homoleptic and heteroleptic complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to Werner's theory, the secondary valence of the central metal ion in a complex corresponds to its coordination number.
Statement II: In [Co(en)₃]Cl₃ (en = ethane-1,2-diamine), the secondary valence of cobalt is 3.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Werner's secondary valence is the coordination number. Each en is didentate, so three en ligands supply six donor nitrogen atoms: the coordination number (secondary valence) of cobalt is 6. Its primary valence (oxidation state) is 3.
steps: Statement I: true (secondary valence = coordination number)
Statement II: false; 3 en × 2 donor atoms = 6, so the secondary valence is 6
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory; coordination number
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the ligand in List-I with the donor atom(s) through which it binds the metal in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ethane-1,2-diamine (en)
B. Oxalate ion, C₂O₄²⁻
C. Carbonyl, CO
D. Nitrite ion, bound as nitrito-O

List-II:
I. One oxygen atom
II. Two nitrogen atoms
III. One carbon atom
IV. Two oxygen atoms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: en, H₂N–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂, is didentate through its two nitrogen atoms; oxalate is didentate through two oxygen atoms; CO binds through carbon; the ambidentate nitrite ion binds through oxygen in the nitrito-O form.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that give oxalate a single oxygen confuse it with nitrito-O; code with CO → one O forgets that CO donates the lone pair on carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', ligands: didentate and ambidentate ligands
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ and [Co(NH₃)₅(SO₄)]Br are ionisation isomers. 0.010 mol of each is dissolved together in water and an excess of BaCl₂ solution is added. The mass of BaSO₄ precipitated is (Ba = 137, S = 32, O = 16):

solution.concept: Ionisation isomers give different ions in solution
solution.explanation: In [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ the sulphate is a counter ion and is free in solution, so it is precipitated by Ba²⁺. In [Co(NH₃)₅(SO₄)]Br the sulphate is coordinated to cobalt and is not available; this isomer gives free Br⁻ instead.
steps: Free SO₄²⁻ comes only from [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄: 0.010 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.66 g assumes that both isomers release sulphate; 1.17 g halves the correct amount; 0 g assumes that sulphate is never free in a cobalt ammine complex.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', structural isomerism: ionisation isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the octahedral complex [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ (Z of Cr = 24), the crystal field splitting energy Δo is 260 kJ mol⁻¹. Taking the energy of each t₂g electron as −0.4Δo and of each eg electron as +0.6Δo, the crystal field stabilisation energy of the complex is:

solution.concept: Crystal field stabilisation energy of a d³ ion
solution.explanation: Cr³⁺ is 3d³. In an octahedral field the three electrons occupy the t₂g orbitals singly (t₂g³ eg⁰), whatever the field strength, so CFSE = 3 × (−0.4Δo) = −1.2Δo.
solution.why_others_wrong: −104 kJ mol⁻¹ counts only one electron; −156 kJ mol⁻¹ uses 0.6Δo for a single electron; −468 kJ mol⁻¹ uses 0.6Δo for each of the three electrons, the eg value, with a minus sign.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): [Mn(CN)₆]³⁻ has two unpaired electrons, whereas [MnCl₆]³⁻ has four unpaired electrons (Z of Mn = 25).
Reason (R): CN⁻ is a strong field ligand that makes two of the four 3d electrons of Mn³⁺ pair up, whereas Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand that cannot do so.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Magnetic behaviour of inner and outer orbital complexes
solution.explanation: Mn³⁺ is 3d⁴. With CN⁻ the electrons pair into three 3d orbitals (two unpaired), leaving two 3d orbitals for d²sp³ hybridisation. With Cl⁻ no pairing occurs, so four electrons stay unpaired and the outer 4d orbitals are used (sp³d²). The ligand field strength is exactly why the numbers differ.
steps: CN⁻ (strong field): paired → 2 unpaired, inner orbital
Cl⁻ (weak field): unpaired → 4 unpaired, outer orbital
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', magnetic properties of coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements, based on valence bond theory, are correct?

(a) dsp² hybridisation of the central atom gives a square planar coordination entity.
(b) sp³d hybridisation of the central atom gives a trigonal bipyramidal coordination entity.
(c) In [CoF₆]³⁻, the six 3d electrons of Co³⁺ are paired up in three 3d orbitals.
(d) An inner orbital complex uses (n−1)d orbitals in hybridisation, whereas an outer orbital complex uses nd orbitals.
(e) Every inner orbital octahedral complex is diamagnetic.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Hybridisation, geometry and inner/outer orbital complexes
solution.explanation: dsp² → square planar and sp³d → trigonal bipyramidal. In [CoF₆]³⁻, F⁻ is a weak field ligand: the 3d⁶ electrons stay unpaired as far as possible (four unpaired) and cobalt uses sp³d² hybrid orbitals. Inner orbital complexes use (n−1)d orbitals, but they need not be diamagnetic: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has one and [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ three unpaired electrons.
steps: (c) false: [CoF₆]³⁻ has four unpaired electrons (outer orbital)
(e) false: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ and [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ are inner orbital yet paramagnetic
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (e) forget paramagnetic inner orbital complexes; options with (c) treat F⁻ as a strong field ligand; (a) and (d) only leaves out the correct shape for sp³d.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory; magnetic properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Werner also studied platinum(IV) ammine chlorides. Assume that platinum has a coordination number of 6 in each compound below and that each is treated with an excess of AgNO₃ solution. Match the compound in List-I with the number of moles of AgCl precipitated per mole of compound in List-II.

List-I:
A. PtCl₄·6NH₃
B. PtCl₄·5NH₃
C. PtCl₄·4NH₃
D. PtCl₄·3NH₃

List-II:
I. 1
II. 2
III. 3
IV. 4

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: With six positions to fill, every NH₃ is coordinated and the remaining positions are taken by chloride ions; only the chlorides outside the coordination sphere are precipitated by Ag⁺.
solution.why_others_wrong: The reversed code takes the coordinated chlorides as the ionisable ones; the other codes pair a compound with a count that leaves the coordination number different from 6.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory of coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ is obtained in a yellow form, in which the nitrite ligand is bound through nitrogen, and in a red form, in which it is bound through oxygen.
Statement II: According to Werner, the ions or groups bound to the metal by secondary linkages have characteristic spatial arrangements corresponding to different coordination numbers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the two linkage isomers of [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂: the yellow –NO₂ (nitrito-N) form and the red –ONO (nitrito-O) form. Werner's postulates include that secondary linkages give characteristic spatial arrangements, the coordination polyhedra (octahedral, tetrahedral, square planar).
steps: Statement I: true (linkage isomers, yellow N-bound and red O-bound)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', linkage isomerism; Werner's theory
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: CrCl₃·6H₂O (molar mass 266.5 g mol⁻¹) exists as hydrate (solvate) isomers in which chromium has a coordination number of 6. A solution containing 2.665 g of one isomer gives 2.87 g of AgCl with an excess of AgNO₃ solution (molar mass of AgCl = 143.5 g mol⁻¹). The isomer is:

solution.concept: Identifying a hydrate isomer from the ionisable chloride
solution.explanation: Only chloride ions outside the coordination sphere are precipitated as AgCl. The mole ratio AgCl : complex tells how many chlorides are ionisable; the rest are coordinated, and water fills the remaining positions.
solution.why_others_wrong: [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ would give 3 mol AgCl per mole (4.31 g); [Cr(H₂O)₄Cl₂]Cl·2H₂O would give 1.435 g; the neutral [Cr(H₂O)₃Cl₃]·3H₂O gives no precipitate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', solvate (hydrate) isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the compound [Cr(NH₃)₆][Fe(CN)₆], chromium is in the +3 oxidation state, and the cyanido complex of iron is low spin (atomic numbers: Cr 24, Fe 26). The total number of unpaired electrons in one formula unit is:

solution.concept: Charge balance and spin state in a complex salt
solution.explanation: The cation is [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺, so the anion must be [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, which contains Fe³⁺ (3d⁵). Cr³⁺ (3d³, t₂g³) has three unpaired electrons; low-spin Fe³⁺ (t₂g⁵) has one.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 treats the anion as [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ with diamagnetic Fe²⁺ (charge does not balance); 5 counts only a high-spin Fe³⁺; 8 adds a high-spin Fe³⁺ (5) to Cr³⁺ (3).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory; magnetic properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which pair of complexes has the same number of unpaired electrons AND the same type of hybridisation of the central atom, according to valence bond theory? ([Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is a high-spin complex; atomic numbers: Cr 24, Mn 25, Fe 26, Co 27, Ni 28.)

solution.explanation: Co³⁺ and Fe²⁺ are both 3d⁶. With the weak field ligands F⁻ and H₂O, both keep four unpaired electrons and use outer 4d orbitals: sp³d², octahedral, four unpaired electrons each.
steps: Other pairs differ in one of the two properties
solution.why_others_wrong: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (dsp²) and [Ni(CO)₄] (sp³) are both diamagnetic but differently hybridised; [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ (1 unpaired) and [Mn(CN)₆]³⁻ (2 unpaired) are both d²sp³; [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ (3) and [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ (0) are both d²sp³.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): [Co(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻ is an outer orbital (sp³d²) complex with four unpaired electrons (Z of Co = 27).
Reason (R): In the spectrochemical series, the oxalate ion lies before water, i.e. it is a weaker field ligand than water.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT reports [Co(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻ as diamagnetic: the six 3d electrons of Co³⁺ are paired, and cobalt uses d²sp³ hybrid orbitals (inner orbital complex). So A is false. R is true: in the spectrochemical series C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O. Even so, Co³⁺ (high charge) gives a splitting large enough for pairing with oxalate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', magnetic properties; spectrochemical series
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Ignoring pairing energy, and taking the energy of each t₂g electron as −0.4Δo and of each eg electron as +0.6Δo in an octahedral field, which of the following statements are correct?

(a) For high-spin [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ (t₂g³ eg²), the crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE) is zero.
(b) A d¹⁰ ion such as Zn²⁺ has zero CFSE in an octahedral field.
(c) A high-spin d⁴ octahedral complex has a CFSE of −0.6Δo.
(d) A low-spin d⁵ octahedral complex has a CFSE of −2.4Δo.
(e) For the same Δo, the magnitude of the CFSE of a high-spin d⁵ ion is larger than that of a high-spin d⁴ ion.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: CFSE = −0.4Δo × (t₂g electrons) + 0.6Δo × (eg electrons).
steps: (e) high-spin d⁵ has 0, high-spin d⁴ has −0.6Δo → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (d) use the low-spin d⁶ value for d⁵; the option with (e) reverses the comparison; (b), (d) and (e) misses two correct statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Kjeldahl's method is to be used to estimate nitrogen. For how many of the following compounds is the method applicable?
Urea, ethanamide (CH₃CONH₂), aniline, nitrobenzene, pyridine, azobenzene (C₆H₅–N=N–C₆H₅)

solution.explanation: In Kjeldahl's method the nitrogen is converted into ammonium sulphate by heating with concentrated H₂SO₄. The method is not applicable to compounds containing nitrogen in nitro and azo groups or in a ring (such as pyridine), because their nitrogen does not change to ammonium sulphate under these conditions.
steps: Not applicable: nitrobenzene (nitro), pyridine (ring N), azobenzene (azo)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 usually leaves out aniline, whose –NH₂ nitrogen is converted normally; 4 or 6 forget the NCERT exclusions for nitro, azo and ring nitrogen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of nitrogen: Kjeldahl's method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In differential extraction, if the organic compound is only slightly soluble in the organic solvent, a very large quantity of solvent would be needed to extract even a small quantity of the compound. The technique used in such cases, in which the same solvent is used repeatedly for extraction, is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: when the compound is less soluble in the organic solvent, the technique of continuous extraction is employed, in which the same solvent is repeatedly used for extraction of the compound.
steps: Low solubility in the organic solvent → large volume needed
Solution: re-use the same solvent repeatedly → continuous extraction
solution.why_others_wrong: Simple and steam distillation separate liquids by volatility; sublimation separates a sublimable solid from a non-sublimable one. None of them reuses an extracting solvent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', differential extraction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: If 0.30 g of urea, CO(NH₂)₂, were analysed by Dumas' method, the volume of nitrogen gas collected, corrected to STP, would be (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22400 mL):

solution.concept: Dumas' method: all nitrogen is collected as N₂
solution.explanation: In Dumas' method the nitrogen of the compound is set free as N₂ gas. One molecule of urea has two nitrogen atoms, which give one molecule of N₂.
steps: N₂ formed = 0.0050 mol (2 N per urea → 1 N₂)
solution.why_others_wrong: 56 mL treats urea as having one nitrogen atom; 224 mL counts one N₂ per nitrogen atom; 448 mL also doubles the moles of urea.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of nitrogen: Dumas method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: 0.239 g of chloroform, CHCl₃, is analysed by the Carius method. Assuming that all its chlorine is converted into silver chloride, the mass of AgCl obtained is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108):

solution.explanation: In the Carius method the halogen of the compound is converted into silver halide. Each molecule of CHCl₃ gives three molecules of AgCl.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.287 g counts one chlorine atom per molecule and 0.574 g two; 1.148 g counts four, as for CCl₄.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of halogens: Carius method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Match the method of quantitative estimation in List-I with the quantity that is finally measured in List-II.

List-I:
A. Dumas' method for nitrogen
B. Kjeldahl's method for nitrogen
C. Carius method for halogens
D. Carius method for sulphur

List-II:
I. Volume of nitrogen gas collected over aqueous KOH
II. Mass of barium sulphate
III. Amount of ammonia absorbed in a known volume of standard acid
IV. Mass of silver halide

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Dumas: nitrogen is collected as N₂ gas over KOH solution. Kjeldahl: nitrogen is converted to ammonium sulphate, the ammonia set free by alkali is absorbed in standard acid, and the unused acid is titrated. Carius: halogen is weighed as silver halide; sulphur is oxidised to sulphuric acid and weighed as barium sulphate.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that swap Dumas and Kjeldahl confuse gas collection with acid absorption; codes that swap the two Carius estimations give sulphur as the silver salt.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: 0.259 g of bromochloromethane, CH₂BrCl, is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate in a Carius tube. Assuming complete conversion of both halogens, the total mass of the silver halide precipitate is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5, Br = 80, Ag = 108):

solution.explanation: Each molecule of CH₂BrCl gives one AgCl and one AgBr. The precipitate is a mixture of the two silver halides.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.574 g treats both halogens as chlorine and 0.752 g both as bromine; 1.326 g doubles the moles of compound.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of halogens: Carius method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In fractional distillation, the vapour that reaches the top of the fractionating column is richer in the more volatile component.
Reason (R): The fractionating column provides many surfaces for heat exchange between the ascending vapours and the descending condensed liquid, so at each stage part of the less volatile component condenses and returns towards the flask.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the fractionating column provides many surfaces for heat exchange between the ascending vapours and the descending condensed liquid. Some of the condensing liquid takes heat from the rising vapours and vaporises, so the vapours become richer in the low-boiling component. Each such condensation and vaporisation unit is a theoretical plate. R is the reason for A.
steps: Repeated condensation and vaporisation along the column
Less volatile component condenses and runs back; vapour at the top is enriched in the more volatile one
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', fractional distillation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Aromatic compounds that contain one or more benzene rings are called benzenoid aromatic compounds. How many of the following are benzenoid aromatic compounds?
Benzene, toluene, naphthalene, pyridine, furan, cyclohexane, tropolone

solution.explanation: Benzenoid aromatic compounds contain a benzene ring: benzene, toluene and naphthalene (two fused benzene rings). Pyridine and furan are heterocyclic aromatic compounds, tropolone is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound and cyclohexane is alicyclic.
steps: Not benzenoid: pyridine, furan (heterocyclic), tropolone (non-benzenoid), cyclohexane (alicyclic)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 leaves out naphthalene, whose fused rings are both benzene rings; 4 or 5 count pyridine or tropolone, which are aromatic but not benzenoid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', classification of organic compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: In ketene, CH₂=C=O, the hybridisation states of the CH₂ carbon and of the central carbon are, respectively:

solution.concept: Hybridisation from the number of σ bonds and π bonds
solution.explanation: The CH₂ carbon forms three σ bonds (two C–H, one C–C) and one π bond: sp². The central carbon forms two double bonds (two σ and two π bonds): sp, like the central carbon of an allene.
solution.why_others_wrong: sp and sp² reverses the two carbons; sp² for the central carbon ignores its second π bond; sp³ would need four σ bonds and no π bond.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', shapes of carbon compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–C(CH₃)=CH–CH₂–CH₃ is:

solution.explanation: The longest chain containing the double bond has five carbons. It is numbered from the end nearer the double bond, so the double bond starts at C-2 and the methyl group is on C-2.
steps: Parent: pentene; number from the left: C1–C2(=C3)
solution.why_others_wrong: 4-Methylpent-3-ene and 2-methylpent-3-ene number the chain from the wrong end, giving the double bond a higher locant; 4-methylpent-2-ene is a different compound, CH₃–CH=CH–CH(CH₃)–CH₃.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The members of a homologous series can be represented by a general formula, and successive members differ from each other by a –CH₂– unit.
Statement II: Alicyclic compounds, such as cyclohexane, show some properties similar to those of aliphatic compounds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A homologous series is a group of compounds with the same functional group, represented by a general formula, in which successive members differ by –CH₂–. NCERT notes that alicyclic (closed-chain, non-aromatic) compounds exhibit some properties similar to those of aliphatic compounds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', classification of organic compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Alkyl free radicals are highly reactive species.
Reason (R): The carbon atom of an alkyl free radical carries an unpaired electron and has only seven electrons in its valence shell, so it readily reacts to pair up this electron.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Homolytic cleavage gives free radicals, in which a carbon atom carries an unpaired electron. With an incomplete octet, the radical reacts at once (for example with Cl₂ or another radical) to pair the electron, so free radicals are short-lived, highly reactive intermediates. R explains A.
steps: R: true; the unpaired electron/incomplete octet is the cause
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', homolytic cleavage; free radicals
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?

solution.explanation: Geometrical isomerism about a C=C bond needs each doubly bonded carbon to carry two different groups. In ClCH=CH–CH₃, C-1 has H and Cl and C-2 has H and CH₃.
steps: ClCH=CHCH₃: both carbons carry two different groups → cis and trans
Other three: one doubly bonded carbon carries two identical groups
solution.why_others_wrong: 2-Chloro- and 3-chloroprop-1-ene have a =CH₂ end (two H atoms); 1,1-dichloroprop-1-ene has two Cl atoms on the same carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', stereoisomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which of the following does heterolytic cleavage of the indicated bond normally leave the shared pair of electrons on carbon, giving a carbanion?

options.text: The C–O bond of protonated ethanol, CH₃CH₂–OH₂⁺

solution.explanation: In heterolysis the shared pair goes to the more electronegative atom. Carbon is more electronegative than magnesium, so in a Grignard reagent the polar C–Mg bond leaves the electron pair on carbon (carbanion character). With Br, O or Cl, the more electronegative atom takes the pair and a carbocation forms.
steps: C–Mg: carbon is the more electronegative atom → carbanion
C–Br, C–O, C–Cl: the heteroatom takes the pair → carbocation
solution.why_others_wrong: Bromoethane, protonated ethanol and tert-butyl chloride all lose an electronegative leaving group with the bonding pair, leaving a positively charged carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', heterolytic cleavage
solution.final_answer: Option C: The C–Mg bond of CH₃CH₂MgBr

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The C–O bond in CH₃–OH is more polar than the C–S bond in CH₃–SH.
Reason (R): Sulphur is more electronegative than oxygen.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Oxygen is more electronegative than sulphur, so the electronegativity difference, and hence the polarity, is greater for the C–O bond. A is true; R is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', inductive effect; polarity of bonds
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hyperconjugation is possible in the methyl cation, CH₃⁺.
Statement II: Hyperconjugation is also possible in alkenes and alkylarenes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Hyperconjugation is the delocalisation of the σ electrons of a C–H bond of an alkyl group directly attached to an atom of an unsaturated system or to an atom with an unshared p orbital. CH₃⁺ has no alkyl group on the positive carbon (its own C–H bonds lie in the nodal plane of the empty p orbital), so it cannot be stabilised by hyperconjugation. NCERT notes hyperconjugation in alkenes (propene) and alkylarenes.
steps: Statement I: false; no C–H bond adjacent to the cationic carbon
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hyperconjugation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with the type of stereoisomerism it shows in List-II.

List-I:
A. 2-Chlorobutane
B. Pent-2-ene
C. 4-Chloropent-2-ene, CH₃–CH=CH–CHCl–CH₃
D. Propan-2-ol

List-II:
I. Both geometrical and optical isomerism
II. Optical isomerism only
III. Neither
IV. Geometrical isomerism only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Optical isomerism needs a carbon bonded to four different groups; geometrical isomerism needs two different groups on each doubly bonded carbon.
steps: 2-Chlorobutane: C-2 chiral, no C=C → optical only
Pent-2-ene: cis/trans, no chiral carbon → geometrical only
Propan-2-ol: C-2 has two CH₃ groups, no C=C → neither
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that give pent-2-ene optical isomerism look for a chiral carbon that is not there; codes that give propan-2-ol any isomerism overlook its two identical methyl groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', stereoisomerism
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about structural isomerism are correct?

(a) Butan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-1-ol are chain isomers.
(b) Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are position isomers.
(c) Propanal and prop-2-en-1-ol (CH₂=CH–CH₂OH) are functional group isomers.
(d) But-1-ene and 2-methylpropene are position isomers.
(e) Methoxyethane and propan-2-ol are metamers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Chain, position and functional isomers; metamers
solution.explanation: Chain isomers differ in the carbon skeleton; position isomers differ in the position of the substituent or functional group on the same skeleton; functional isomers have different functional groups. Metamerism arises from different alkyl groups on either side of the same functional group.
steps: (a) C₄H₁₀O, straight vs branched chain → true
(c) both C₃H₆O; aldehyde vs alcohol (with C=C) → true
(d) straight vs branched skeleton → chain isomers, false
(e) ether vs alcohol → functional isomers, not metamers, false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) mistake a change of skeleton for a change of position; the option with (e) calls an ether–alcohol pair metamers, although metamers must share the functional group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
For the reaction CH₃CH₂Br + HS⁻ → CH₃CH₂SH + Br⁻, which of the following statements are correct?

(a) HS⁻ acts as the nucleophile.
(b) CH₃CH₂Br is the substrate.
(c) Br⁻ is the leaving group.
(d) The carbon atom attacked by HS⁻ carries a partial negative charge.
(e) The reaction is a substitution reaction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The substrate supplies the carbon to the new bond: here CH₃CH₂Br. The reagent HS⁻ brings an electron pair, so it is a nucleophile, and it attacks the carbon bonded to bromine, which carries a partial positive charge because Br is more electronegative. Br⁻ leaves, and one group replaces another: a substitution.
steps: (d) false: the C–Br carbon is δ+
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (d) reverse the polarity of the C–Br bond; (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the correct classification as substitution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', substrate and reagent; types of organic reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about hybridisation and shape are correct?

(a) In CH₃–C≡N, the carbon of the CH₃ group is sp³ and the nitrile carbon is sp hybridised.
(b) In benzene, all six carbon atoms are sp² hybridised.
(c) An sp² hybridised carbon is more electronegative than an sp³ hybridised carbon.
(d) In propyne, CH₃–C≡CH, the C–C≡C bond angle is 120°.
(e) In the carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺, the positively charged carbon is sp³ hybridised.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A carbon with four σ bonds is sp³, with one π bond sp², and with two π bonds sp. Greater s character makes the carbon more electronegative (sp > sp² > sp³). The sp carbons of an alkyne are linear (180°). The positive carbon of a carbocation uses three sp² orbitals and has an empty p orbital.
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) uses the sp² angle for sp carbons; (e) gives a carbocation the hybridisation of a carbanion; options containing either are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation; carbocations

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are functional group isomers of propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH?
Methyl ethanoate, ethyl methanoate, propanal, 2-hydroxypropanal (CH₃CH(OH)CHO), ethanoic acid, propan-1-ol, propane-1,2-diol

solution.concept: Functional group isomers: same molecular formula, different functional group
solution.explanation: Propanoic acid is C₃H₆O₂. A functional group isomer must have the same molecular formula but a different functional group. Check the formula of each compound first.
steps: C₃H₆O₂: methyl ethanoate, ethyl methanoate (esters), 2-hydroxypropanal (aldehyde + alcohol) → isomers
Propanal C₃H₆O, ethanoic acid C₂H₄O₂, propan-1-ol C₃H₈O, propane-1,2-diol C₃H₈O₂ → not isomers
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only the two esters and misses the hydroxy aldehyde; lower counts also judge by functional group alone without checking the molecular formula.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', functional group isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of HOOC–CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂–C≡N is:

solution.concept: Principal functional group, prefixes and alphabetical order
solution.explanation: –COOH ranks above –CN, so the compound is named as a butanoic acid (C-1 = COOH, chain of four carbons). The –C≡N group, cited as a prefix (cyano), is not counted in the parent chain. Prefixes are cited alphabetically: cyano before hydroxy.
steps: Principal group –COOH → '-oic acid'; parent chain C1–C4 = butanoic acid
Substituents: OH on C-3, CN on C-4
solution.why_others_wrong: '3-Hydroxy-4-cyano' breaks the alphabetical order; 'pentanoic acid' counts the nitrile carbon both in the chain and in the prefix; naming it as a nitrile ignores the higher priority of –COOH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of polyfunctional compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the tert-butyl cation, (CH₃)₃C⁺, the positively charged carbon and the three carbon atoms attached to it lie in one plane.
Reason (R): The tert-butyl cation is more stable than the isopropyl cation, (CH₃)₂CH⁺.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The planarity comes from the sp² hybridisation of the positive carbon: its three σ bonds lie in one plane at 120°, with the vacant p orbital perpendicular to it. R is a true but separate property: tert-butyl is more stable than isopropyl because of more hyperconjugation and +I effect of three methyl groups. Stability does not decide the shape (the isopropyl cation is planar too).
steps: R does not explain the planar shape
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', carbocations
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: 2,3-Dimethylbutane and 2,2-dimethylbutane are chain isomers.
Statement II: Pentan-2-one and 3-methylbutan-2-one are position isomers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both pairs are C₆H₁₄ and C₅H₁₀O isomers respectively. 2,3- and 2,2-dimethylbutane differ in the carbon skeleton, so they are chain isomers. Pentan-2-one (straight chain) and 3-methylbutan-2-one (branched chain) also differ in the skeleton, with the C=O at C-2 in both; they are chain isomers, not position isomers.
steps: Statement II: false; different skeletons → chain isomers
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the structure in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₂=CH–CH₂–C≡N
B. HC≡C–CH₂–CH₂–OH
C. CH₃–CO–CH₂–CHO
D. HO–CH₂–CH₂–COO–CH₃

List-II:
I. Methyl 3-hydroxypropanoate
II. 3-Oxobutanal
III. But-3-enenitrile
IV. But-3-yn-1-ol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The principal group decides the suffix and gets the lowest locant; the nitrile carbon is C-1 of the chain; the –CHO carbon is C-1 and a ketonic C=O is cited as 'oxo'; esters are named alkyl alkanoate.
steps: CH₂=CH–CH₂–CN: C1 = CN, C=C at 3 → but-3-enenitrile
HC≡C–CH₂–CH₂OH: C1 bears OH, C≡C at 3 → but-3-yn-1-ol
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that swap the ester and the oxo-aldehyde mistake a –COO– group for a ketone; codes that swap the nitrile and the alkynol ignore which group carries C-1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about carbocations are correct?

(a) In CH₃CH₂⁺, the C–H bonds of the CH₃ group, not those on the positively charged carbon, take part in hyperconjugation.
(b) The benzyl cation, C₆H₅CH₂⁺, is stabilised by delocalisation of its positive charge over the benzene ring.
(c) The isopropyl cation, (CH₃)₂CH⁺, has six C–H bonds that can take part in hyperconjugation.
(d) Carbocations behave as nucleophiles because they carry a positive charge.
(e) The order of stability of carbocations is CH₃⁺ > CH₃CH₂⁺ > (CH₃)₂CH⁺.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Hyperconjugation uses C–H bonds on carbons adjacent to the positive carbon: three in CH₃CH₂⁺ and six in (CH₃)₂CH⁺. Benzylic and allylic carbocations are stabilised by resonance. Carbocations are electron deficient and act as electrophiles; their stability order is 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) confuse electron-deficient species with nucleophiles; the option with (e) reverses the stability order.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', carbocations; hyperconjugation; resonance

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 7.8 g of benzene is heated with fuming sulphuric acid (oleum) and is converted completely into benzenesulphonic acid, C₆H₅SO₃H. The mass of benzenesulphonic acid formed is (C = 12, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16):

solution.explanation: Benzene reacts with fuming sulphuric acid to give benzenesulphonic acid: C₆H₆ + SO₃ (H₂SO₄) → C₆H₅SO₃H. One mole of benzene gives one mole of product.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8.0 g is the mass of SO₃ used; 7.8 g simply repeats the mass of benzene; 23.8 g is for a disulphonic acid, C₆H₄(SO₃H)₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', electrophilic substitution reactions: sulphonation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the free radical chlorination of methane in light, which of the following is a chain propagation step?

solution.explanation: Initiation: homolysis of Cl₂ by light. Propagation: a chlorine radical abstracts H from methane to give a methyl radical and HCl; the methyl radical then reacts with Cl₂ to give CH₃Cl and a new chlorine radical. Termination: two radicals combine.
steps: CH₄ + Cl• → CH₃• + HCl: propagation (radical in, radical out)
solution.why_others_wrong: Homolysis of Cl₂ starts the chain (initiation); Cl• + Cl• and CH₃• + CH₃• consume radicals without forming new ones, so they end the chain (termination).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: halogenation mechanism
solution.final_answer: Option D: CH₄ + Cl• → CH₃• + HCl

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An aqueous solution of sodium propanoate, CH₃CH₂COONa, is electrolysed by Kolbe's electrolytic method. The hydrocarbon formed at the anode is:

solution.explanation: In Kolbe's electrolysis 2RCOONa + 2H₂O → R–R + 2CO₂ + H₂ + 2NaOH. The alkyl groups of two carboxylate ions join after losing CO₂. With R = C₂H₅, the product is C₂H₅–C₂H₅, butane.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ethane is formed from sodium ethanoate; propane would need the carboxyl carbon to stay in the chain; hexane would need two propyl groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkanes from carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ozonolysis is used to locate the position of the double bond in an alkene.
Reason (R): On ozonolysis followed by treatment with zinc and water, the alkene is cleaved at the double bond, and each carbon that was part of the double bond becomes the carbon of a C=O group in the products.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Because the molecule is cut exactly at the C=C bond and both doubly bonded carbons end up as carbonyl carbons, identifying the carbonyl products tells where the double bond was. R is the reason for A.
steps: Alkene + O₃ → ozonide; Zn/H₂O → two carbonyl compounds
Carbonyl carbons = former doubly bonded carbons → position of C=C
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: ozonolysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ethyne adds one molecule of HBr to give bromoethene, which adds a second molecule of HBr to give 1,1-dibromoethane.
Statement II: Propyne, on hydration with dilute H₂SO₄ in the presence of Hg²⁺ ions, gives propanal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: HBr adds to ethyne first to give CH₂=CHBr; the second addition follows Markovnikov's rule, putting Br on the carbon that already carries Br: CH₃CHBr₂ (1,1-dibromoethane). Hydration of propyne also follows Markovnikov's rule: the enol CH₃C(OH)=CH₂ changes into propanone, not propanal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: addition of hydrogen halides and water
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 18.8 g of 1,2-dibromoethane is heated with zinc dust and is converted completely into ethene. The volume of ethene formed, measured at STP, is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.explanation: Vicinal dihalides lose both halogen atoms on heating with zinc: BrCH₂–CH₂Br + Zn → CH₂=CH₂ + ZnBr₂. One mole of dihalide gives one mole of ethene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.48 L assumes two moles of gas per mole of dihalide; 1.12 L halves the moles; 0.224 L misplaces the decimal (0.01 mol).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkenes from vicinal dihalides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 0.10 mol of methane is chlorinated in diffused sunlight, and the methane is converted completely into an equimolar mixture of CH₃Cl and CH₂Cl₂ only. The amount of HCl formed is:

solution.explanation: Each hydrogen atom replaced by chlorine gives one molecule of HCl: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl and CH₄ + 2Cl₂ → CH₂Cl₂ + 2HCl.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.10 mol counts one HCl per methane; 0.20 mol counts two for every methane; 0.30 mol counts the chlorine atoms used (0.15 mol Cl₂ = 0.30 mol Cl) instead of the HCl formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: substitution reactions (halogenation)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: With chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light, benzene gives hexachlorobenzene, C₆Cl₆, by substitution.
Statement II: With an excess of chlorine in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ in the dark, benzene can be converted into hexachlorobenzene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In UV light benzene adds three molecules of chlorine to give benzene hexachloride, C₆H₆Cl₆ (an addition product), not hexachlorobenzene. With a Lewis acid and an excess of the electrophilic reagent, substitution continues until all six hydrogens are replaced: C₆H₆ + 6Cl₂ → C₆Cl₆ + 6HCl.
steps: Statement I: false; UV light → C₆H₆Cl₆ by addition
Statement II: true; excess Cl₂ / anhydrous AlCl₃ → C₆Cl₆ by substitution
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons: chemical properties
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the conversion in List-I with the catalyst or conditions used for it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Hydrogenation of an alkene to an alkane
B. Partial hydrogenation of an alkyne to a cis-alkene
C. Hydration of ethyne to ethanal
D. Conversion of n-hexane into benzene

List-II:
I. Hg²⁺ ions in dilute H₂SO₄ at 333 K
II. Cr₂O₃ supported on alumina at 773 K and 10–20 atm
III. Palladium on charcoal partly deactivated with quinoline
IV. Finely divided Pt, Pd or Ni

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alkenes and alkynes are hydrogenated completely over finely divided Pt, Pd or Ni; Lindlar's catalyst (Pd on charcoal deactivated with quinoline) stops the reduction of an alkyne at the cis-alkene; alkynes are hydrated with Hg²⁺/dilute H₂SO₄ at 333 K; n-hexane is aromatised over Cr₂O₃ (or V₂O₅, Mo₂O₃) on alumina at 773 K.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that swap the two palladium/nickel catalysts would reduce an alkyne fully or stop an alkene reaction; codes that swap hydration and aromatisation mix up the mercury catalyst with the oxide catalyst.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation and properties of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about substituents on a benzene ring in electrophilic substitution are correct?

(a) The –COOR group is meta directing.
(b) The –NHCOCH₃ group is ortho and para directing.
(c) The –SO₃H group is ortho and para directing.
(d) The –CN group deactivates the benzene ring.
(e) The –Br group activates the benzene ring.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ortho/para directors: –OH, –NH₂, –NHR, –NHCOCH₃, –OCH₃, –CH₃ and halogens. Meta directors (deactivating): –NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COR, –COOH, –COOR, –SO₃H. Halogens are ortho/para directing but deactivate the ring because of their strong −I effect.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) treat –SO₃H as an electron-releasing group; options with (e) confuse the ortho/para direction of halogens with activation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', directive influence of a functional group in monosubstituted benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The peroxide effect is not observed when HCl adds to propene.
Reason (R): The H–Cl bond is weaker than the H–Br bond, so HCl is readily cleaved by free radicals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why only HBr shows the peroxide effect
solution.explanation: NCERT explains that the H–Cl bond (430.5 kJ mol⁻¹) is stronger than the H–Br bond (363.7 kJ mol⁻¹) and is not cleaved by the free radicals formed from the peroxide. So A is true and R, which reverses the bond strengths, is false.
steps: R: false; H–Cl is stronger than H–Br
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: anti-Markovnikov addition (peroxide effect)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.2 g of propene is treated with HBr in the absence of peroxide, and the product is heated with sodium in dry ether. Assuming every step is complete, the final hydrocarbon and its mass are (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Markovnikov addition followed by the Wurtz reaction
solution.explanation: Without peroxide, HBr adds by Markovnikov's rule to give 2-bromopropane. In the Wurtz reaction two isopropyl groups join: (CH₃)₂CH–CH(CH₃)₂, 2,3-dimethylbutane. Two moles of alkyl halide give one mole of alkane.
solution.why_others_wrong: n-Hexane would come from 1-bromopropane (peroxide addition); 8.6 g forgets that two molecules of alkyl halide give one molecule of alkane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', Markovnikov rule; Wurtz reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
HBr is added to each of the following alkenes, once in the absence and once in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. For how many of them is the main product the same in both cases?
Ethene, propene, but-1-ene, but-2-ene, 2-methylpropene, cyclohexene, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene

solution.concept: Peroxide effect matters only for unsymmetrical alkenes
solution.explanation: Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov additions give different products only when the two doubly bonded carbons are differently substituted. For a symmetrical alkene, Br goes to an equivalent carbon either way.
steps: Symmetrical: ethene, but-2-ene, cyclohexene, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene → same product (4)
solution.why_others_wrong: Lower counts usually leave out cyclohexene or 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, whose doubly bonded carbons are equivalent even though the molecules are not straight chains.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: addition of hydrogen halides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: m-Bromonitrobenzene is to be prepared from benzene as the main product, using Br₂/FeBr₃ and a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄. The correct sequence is:

options.text: Either order, as both give the same main product
Both reagents together in a single step

solution.explanation: The –NO₂ group is meta directing, so brominating nitrobenzene puts Br at the meta position. Bromine is ortho/para directing, so nitrating bromobenzene would give mainly o- and p-bromonitrobenzene.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bromination first gives ortho and para products; the order matters because the first group directs the second; a one-step mixture gives no control over position.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', directive influence of a functional group in monosubstituted benzene
solution.final_answer: Option A: Nitration first, then bromination

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Each alkene in List-I is hydrated with water in the presence of an acid. Match it with its main product in List-II.

List-I:
A. Propene
B. 2-Methylpropene
C. But-1-ene
D. Ethene

List-II:
I. Ethanol
II. Butan-2-ol
III. Propan-2-ol
IV. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Acid-catalysed hydration goes through the more stable carbocation, so the –OH ends up on the more substituted carbon of the double bond (Markovnikov's rule).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes give an alcohol whose carbon skeleton differs from that of the alkene (for example ethene → butan-2-ol or propene → 2-methylpropan-2-ol); the trap in this set is but-1-ene, which gives butan-2-ol, not butan-1-ol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: addition of water
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the addition of HBr to propene are correct?

(a) In the absence of peroxide, the first step is the attack of H⁺, an electrophile, on the double bond.
(b) Protonation at C-1 gives a secondary carbocation, which is formed in preference to the primary one.
(c) In the second step, Br⁻ attacks the carbocation.
(d) In the presence of a peroxide, a bromine free radical adds first to C-1, giving the more stable secondary free radical.
(e) The addition in the presence of a peroxide proceeds through a carbocation intermediate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Mechanisms of Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov addition
solution.explanation: Ionic addition: H⁺ adds to C-1 to give the 2° carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃, which Br⁻ attacks → 2-bromopropane. Peroxide addition is a free radical chain: Br• adds to C-1, giving the 2° radical CH₃ĊHCH₂Br, which takes H from HBr → 1-bromopropane. No carbocation is involved in the peroxide reaction.
solution.why_others_wrong: (a), (b) and (c) only misses the radical step; options with (e) attribute a carbocation to the free radical pathway.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: mechanism of addition of HBr

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 7.4 g of 2-methylpropan-2-ol is shaken with concentrated hydrochloric acid at room temperature and is converted completely into 2-chloro-2-methylpropane. The mass of the alkyl chloride formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Preparation of a tertiary alkyl chloride from an alcohol
solution.explanation: Tertiary alcohols react with concentrated HCl even at room temperature: (CH₃)₃C–OH + HCl → (CH₃)₃C–Cl + H₂O. One mole of alcohol gives one mole of alkyl chloride.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.65 g is the mass of HCl consumed; 7.40 g repeats the mass of the alcohol; 13.7 g uses the molar mass of the bromide, C₄H₉Br.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of benzyl chloride, C₆H₅CH₂Cl, is:

solution.explanation: In C₆H₅CH₂Cl the chlorine is on the side-chain carbon, not on the ring. The substituent –CH₂Cl on benzene is named chloromethyl, so the compound is (chloromethyl)benzene.
steps: Cl on the CH₂ group attached to the ring
solution.why_others_wrong: 1-Chloro-2-methylbenzene and 1-chloro-4-methylbenzene are chlorotoluenes, with chlorine on the ring; chlorobenzene, C₆H₅Cl, has no CH₂ group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Exposure to lower levels of dichloromethane in air can lead to slightly impaired hearing and vision.
Statement II: Exposure to carbon tetrachloride can make the heart beat irregularly or stop.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that lower levels of methylene chloride in air can lead to slightly impaired hearing and vision, and that exposure to carbon tetrachloride can make the heart beat irregularly or stop (besides liver damage and effects on the nervous system).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds: dichloromethane, tetrachloromethane
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reagent in List-I, reacting with a haloalkane R–X, with the main organic product in List-II.

List-I:
A. A primary amine, R′NH₂
B. Silver cyanide, AgCN
C. Potassium nitrite, KNO₂
D. Silver salt of a carboxylic acid, R′COOAg

List-II:
I. Alkyl nitrite, R–O–N=O
II. Isocyanide, R–NC
III. Ester, R′COOR
IV. Secondary amine, R–NH–R′

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A primary amine attacks through nitrogen to give a secondary amine; AgCN, being mainly covalent, attacks through nitrogen to give an isocyanide; KNO₂ (ionic) attacks through oxygen to give an alkyl nitrite; the carboxylate ion of a silver salt gives an ester.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping AgCN and the amine mixes up an isocyanide and an amine; swapping KNO₂ with AgCN or the silver carboxylate confuses the ambident nitrite attack with other reagents.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution reactions
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.6 g of ethanol is converted completely into chloroethane by heating with thionyl chloride. The total volume of the gaseous by-products, measured at STP, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.explanation: C₂H₅OH + SOCl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑. Both by-products are gases, which is why this method gives a fairly pure alkyl chloride.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.24 L counts only one of the two gases; 6.72 L also counts chloroethane, which is the product and not a by-product; 1.12 L halves one gas.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation from alcohols: thionyl chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 11.25 g of chlorobenzene is treated with sodium in dry ether, and the Fittig reaction goes to completion. The mass of biphenyl, C₆H₅–C₆H₅, formed is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.explanation: Aryl halides couple with sodium in dry ether: 2C₆H₅Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅–C₆H₅ + 2NaCl. Two moles of aryl halide give one mole of biphenyl.
solution.why_others_wrong: 15.4 g forgets that two aryl groups make one biphenyl; 3.85 g halves twice; 11.25 g repeats the mass of chlorobenzene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reactions of haloarenes with metals: Fittig reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Alkyl chlorides are converted into alkyl iodides by heating with NaI in dry acetone.
Reason (R): The NaCl formed is precipitated in dry acetone, which drives the reaction forward according to Le Chatelier's principle.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: R–Cl + NaI ⇌ R–I + NaCl is an equilibrium. In dry acetone NaI is soluble but NaCl is not; as NaCl precipitates, it is removed from the equilibrium, so the reaction goes to completion. R explains A.
steps: Removal of NaCl as a precipitate shifts the equilibrium to the right
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', halogen exchange
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Alkyl bromides can be prepared from alcohols using red phosphorus and bromine, which generate PBr₃ in situ.
Statement II: Primary alcohols are converted into alkyl chlorides simply by shaking with concentrated HCl at room temperature, without any catalyst.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: PBr₃ and PI₃ are usually generated in situ by the reaction of red phosphorus with bromine or iodine. Only tertiary alcohols react with concentrated HCl at room temperature; primary and secondary alcohols need anhydrous ZnCl₂ as catalyst (and heating).
steps: Statement II: false; this works only for tertiary alcohols
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about polyhalogen compounds are correct?

(a) Chloroform is used as a solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine.
(b) In the stratosphere, freons initiate radical chain reactions that upset the natural ozone balance.
(c) Iodoform is now widely preferred as an antiseptic because of its pleasant smell.
(d) Dichloromethane is used as a propellant in aerosols and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.
(e) DDT has been used to kill mosquitoes that spread malaria and lice that carry typhus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Uses and environmental effects of polyhalogen compounds
solution.explanation: NCERT: chloroform is a solvent for fats, alkaloids and iodine; freons that reach the stratosphere start radical chain reactions upsetting the ozone balance; dichloromethane is a paint remover, aerosol propellant and process solvent for drugs; DDT was used against malaria-spreading mosquitoes and typhus-carrying lice. Iodoform has an objectionable smell and has been replaced by other iodine formulations.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (c) accept the wrong claim about iodoform; (a), (d) and (e) only leaves out the role of freons in ozone depletion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Considering all the structural isomers of the monobromoalkane C₅H₁₁Br, how many of them are secondary (2°) alkyl bromides?

solution.explanation: C₅H₁₁Br has eight structural isomers. An alkyl halide is secondary when the carbon carrying the halogen is bonded to two other carbon atoms.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 usually misses the branched 2-bromo-3-methylbutane; 4 counts 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, which is tertiary; 1 counts only the tertiary bromide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', classification of haloalkanes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reacts fastest with OH⁻ ions by the SN2 mechanism?

solution.explanation: In SN2 the nucleophile attacks the carbon from the side opposite the leaving group, in a single step. Bulky groups on or next to that carbon hinder the attack. 1-Bromopentane is primary with an unbranched chain, so it is attacked most easily.
steps: (CH₃)₃C–CH₂Br: 1°, but the bulky tert-butyl group next to the reacting carbon hinders attack
solution.why_others_wrong: Neopentyl bromide is primary, but the adjacent tert-butyl group blocks the back-side approach; secondary and tertiary bromides are more crowded at the reacting carbon itself.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN2 mechanism: steric effects

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): SN1 reactions of alkyl halides are favoured by non-polar solvents.
Reason (R): In SN1 reactions, polar protic solvents stabilise the carbocation and the leaving halide ion by solvation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The slow step of SN1 is the ionisation of R–X into R⁺ and X⁻. Polar protic solvents such as water, alcohols and ethanoic acid help this step by solvating both ions, so SN1 reactions are generally carried out in polar protic solvents. A is false; R is true.
steps: A: false; SN1 needs polar protic solvents
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about dehydrohalogenation (β-elimination) are correct?

(a) 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane, heated with alcoholic KOH, gives mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene.
(b) 1-Bromobutane, heated with alcoholic KOH, gives but-1-ene.
(c) A tertiary alkyl halide treated with a strong base mainly undergoes SN2 substitution.
(d) 1-Bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane, (CH₃)₃C–CH₂Br, cannot undergo β-elimination, because its β-carbon carries no hydrogen atom.
(e) In dehydrohalogenation, the halogen and a hydrogen atom are removed from the same carbon atom.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In β-elimination, H is lost from the β-carbon (next to the carbon bearing X). Zaitsev's rule: the alkene with more alkyl groups on the doubly bonded carbons is preferred. A tertiary halide with a strong base prefers elimination. In neopentyl bromide the only β-carbon is a quaternary carbon with no hydrogen.
steps: (e) false: H comes from the β-carbon
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) ignore the competition that favours elimination for 3° halides; the option with (e) describes an α-elimination, which is not dehydrohalogenation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.4 g of phenol is heated with zinc dust and is converted completely into benzene. The mass of benzene formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Reduction of phenol by zinc dust
solution.explanation: Phenol is converted into benzene on heating with zinc dust: C₆H₅OH + Zn → C₆H₆ + ZnO. One mole of phenol gives one mole of benzene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 9.4 g repeats the mass of phenol; 3.9 g and 15.6 g halve or double the 1 : 1 mole ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reactions of phenol with zinc dust

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.1 g of ethanenitrile, CH₃CN, is hydrolysed completely with dilute acid. The mass of the carboxylic acid formed is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Preparation of carboxylic acids from nitriles
solution.explanation: Nitriles are hydrolysed, through amides, to carboxylic acids in the presence of H⁺ or OH⁻ as catalyst: CH₃C≡N → CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃COOH. One mole of nitrile gives one mole of acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.9 g stops at the amide, CH₃CONH₂; 4.6 g is the mass of 0.10 mol of ethanol; 4.1 g repeats the mass of the nitrile.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', methods of preparation of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of glycerol, HOCH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂OH, is:

solution.explanation: For a polyol the 'e' of the alkane name is kept and multiplying prefixes are added to 'ol': three –OH groups on a three-carbon chain at C-1, C-2 and C-3 give propane-1,2,3-triol.
solution.why_others_wrong: Propane-1,3-diol has only two –OH groups; 'trihydroxypropane' cites the principal group as a prefix; 'propan-1,2,3-ol' drops the multiplying prefix 'tri' and the 'e'.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the acid-catalysed dehydration of ethanol, the formation of the carbocation is the slowest, rate-determining step.
Statement II: The reaction of an alcohol with an acid chloride to give an ester is carried out in the presence of a base such as pyridine, which neutralises the HCl formed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Dehydration mechanism; esterification with acid chlorides
solution.explanation: Dehydration of ethanol: (1) protonation of the –OH group, (2) loss of water to form the carbocation, the slowest step, (3) loss of a proton to give ethene. In acylation by an acid chloride, HCl is formed; pyridine removes it and shifts the equilibrium forward.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', chemical reactions of alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sodium phenoxide reacts with carbon dioxide, a weak electrophile, and the product on acidification gives salicylic acid.
Reason (R): The phenoxide ion is even more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the phenoxide ion, generated by treating phenol with NaOH, is even more reactive than phenol towards electrophilic substitution, and hence it reacts even with CO₂, a weak electrophile, giving ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) after acidification. R is the reason for A.
steps: –O⁻ is a stronger electron donor than –OH
Strongly activated ring attacks the weak electrophile CO₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', Kolbe's reaction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the common name of the alcohol in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. Isobutyl alcohol
B. tert-Butyl alcohol
C. sec-Butyl alcohol
D. Neopentyl alcohol

List-II:
I. Butan-2-ol
II. 2,2-Dimethylpropan-1-ol
III. 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
IV. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Common and IUPAC names of alcohols
solution.explanation: Isobutyl = (CH₃)₂CHCH₂–; tert-butyl = (CH₃)₃C–; sec-butyl = CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)–; neopentyl = (CH₃)₃CCH₂–.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping isobutyl and tert-butyl confuses a 1° alcohol with a 3° alcohol; swapping sec-butyl and neopentyl confuses a C₄ with a C₅ alcohol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
An acid liberates CO₂ from aqueous sodium hydrogencarbonate only if it is a stronger acid than carbonic acid (pKa = 6.4). Using the pKa values given in brackets, how many of the following liberate CO₂ from NaHCO₃?
Ethanoic acid (4.76), benzoic acid (4.19), methanoic acid (3.75), phenol (10.0), 4-nitrophenol (7.1), picric acid, i.e. 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (0.5), ethanol (15.9)

solution.concept: Acid strength and the hydrogencarbonate test
solution.explanation: A lower pKa means a stronger acid. Acids with pKa below 6.4 are stronger than carbonic acid and displace CO₂ from NaHCO₃.
steps: pKa < 6.4: ethanoic, benzoic, methanoic acids and picric acid → 4
